title: ImageInferenceResult 1.0
description: The body of the message ImageProcessor publishes on `ecv1/{device}/image-processor/{routeId}/app/inference/result`, with header name `ImageInferenceResult` and version `1.0`. This message is the authoritative, cleanup-gating output for one image: it is prepared once, stored byte for byte in the ledger, and published with positive transport confirmation before the input is archived, deleted, or quarantined. A consumer that enforces a safety gate reads this message and nothing else, and treats a missing, failed, stale, or unverified result as not clear. Every collection is bounded; when a result exceeds the message budget the full result is written to the evidence sidecar and this message carries the bounded summary with `outputs.truncated` set and `artifacts` naming the sidecar.

schemaVersion.description: The body contract version. A consumer that does not recognize the version does not interpret the body.

inferenceId.description: The stable identity of this inference, derived once from the route, the capture or source digest, and the model digest. A retry reuses it, and a crash between transport confirmation and the local acknowledgement may publish a duplicate, so consumers deduplicate on this field. Reprocessing under a different model digest produces a different id.

routeId.description: The route that produced the result. It is also the `{instance}` segment of the topic.

status.description: Whether the model produced a result. `SUCCEEDED` carries `decision` and `outputs`; `FAILED` carries `error`, and its decision is never `CLEAR`.

source.title: Input identity
source.description: What was inferred on, and how it arrived.

kind.description: How the image reached the component. `spool`: discovered as a finalized file in a watched root. `inline`: carried as binary bytes in a trigger message and written to processor-owned staging. `reference`: named by a trigger message and resolved under the route's `fileRoot`.

captureId.description: The camera's capture identity, when the input came from a camera spool. It is the preferred half of the job's logical key.

cameraId.description: The camera instance that produced the image.

relativePath.description: The input's path relative to the route's root, with `/` separators. Absolute paths are never published, and a path supplied by a producer is never trusted without containment and digest verification.

bytes.description: The verified size of the input in bytes.

sha256.description: The verified SHA-256 of the input bytes. It is what the executor cell checked before it decoded anything.

correlationId.description: The correlation id of the trigger message, when the job came from a request.

capturedAtMs.description: When the image was captured, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, as reported by the camera.

model.title: Model generation and execution
model.description: The exact model generation that produced the result, and the provider it actually ran on.

id.description: The model's published id, as the bundle manifest declares it.

version.description: The model's published version, as the bundle manifest declares it.

digest.description: The bundle tarball digest the job was pinned to. Two results with the same digest came from bit-identical weights.

runtimeVersion.description: The runtime's version, as reported by the executor cell.

providers.description: The execution providers the session was actually assigned, in the order the runtime reports them. This is the observed assignment, not the configured preference, so a result never implies a GPU it did not use.

gpu.description: The device the session ran on, or `null` on a CPU session.

deviceId.description: The CUDA ordinal or device UUID.

class.description: The device class, used to key measured memory profiles and engine caches.

transformVersion.description: The decode and preprocessing contract version the cell applied. Two results are comparable only when their transform versions match.

decision.title: Decision
decision.description: The decision rules' verdict over the normalized output. A rule that cannot evaluate yields `HOLD`, never `CLEAR`.

outcome.description: The gate verdict. `CLEAR`: the rules evaluated and passed. `HOLD`: the rules did not pass, or could not be evaluated. `FAIL`: the inference itself failed.

pass.description: Whether the pass rule evaluated true. It is `false` whenever `outcome` is not `CLEAR`.

confidence.description: The confidence the rules extracted from the normalized output, or `null` when the rule produced no number.

threshold.description: The threshold the confidence was compared against, as configured in the bundle manifest.

rule.description: The rule expression that decided the outcome, so an operator can see why a result held.

outputs.title: Normalized model output
outputs.description: The task family's output in the shape the decision rules evaluate. Only the family's own collection is populated. Masks and tensors are never published; segmentation reports pixel counts and regions instead.

family.description: The task family the bundle declares, which is what determines the collection below.

classes.description: Classification scores, ordered by descending score and bounded by the manifest's `maxResultItems`.

detections.description: Detections after non-maximum suppression, ordered by descending score and bounded by the manifest's `maxResultItems`.

segments.description: Per-class segmentation summary, keyed by class label.

truncated.description: Whether the collections above were bounded to fit the message budget. When it is `true`, `artifacts` names the sidecar that holds the full result, so a decision-bearing result is never shortened silently.

timings.title: Stage timings
timings.description: Milliseconds spent in each stage of one attempt. `total` covers admission to result commit.

modelLoad.description: Time spent loading the model generation, which is `0` on a resident session.

preprocess.description: Decode, resize, and normalization in the executor cell.

artifacts.title: Evidence artifacts
artifacts.description: The evidence sidecar this result belongs to. It is present whenever the route writes a sidecar, and required whenever the published outputs are truncated.

evidenceId.description: The identity of the evidence record, which is what a downstream evidence chain joins on.

localRelativePath.description: The sidecar's path relative to the route's evidence root, with `/` separators.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the installed sidecar, which is immutable once written.

bytes.description: The size of the sidecar in bytes.

error.title: Failure detail
error.description: Why the inference failed. It is present exactly when `status` is `FAILED`.

message.description: A bounded human-readable diagnostic. It never carries image bytes, tensors, or credentials.

class.description: How the failure is handled. `transient`: retried under the job's retry budget. `permanent`: the input can never succeed, so the job takes the invalid-input completion action. `contaminating`: the executor cell's CUDA context is unusable, so the cell drains and restarts and the job returns to retry.

label.description: The class label from the bundle's label file.

index.description: The class index in the model's output vector.

score.description: The class score after the family's activation.

label.description: The class label from the bundle's label file.

index.description: The class index in the model's output vector.

score.description: The detection score after non-maximum suppression.

box.title: Normalized box
box.description: A box in the source image's coordinate space, normalized to `[0, 1]`, so a consumer needs no knowledge of the model's input resolution.

pixels.description: How many source pixels the class covers.

bbox.description: The bounding region of the class as `[x, y, w, h]`, normalized to `[0, 1]`.

score.description: The model's anomaly score for the image.

threshold.description: The threshold the score is compared against, from the bundle manifest.

summary.title: Heatmap summary
summary.description: A bounded summary of the anomaly heatmap. The heatmap itself is never published.

regions.description: The strongest contiguous regions, ordered by descending score.

bbox.description: The region as `[x, y, w, h]`, normalized to `[0, 1]`.

pixels.description: How many source pixels the region covers.

hex256.description: A SHA-256 digest as 64 lowercase hex characters, without a prefix.

digest.description: A SHA-256 digest in `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` form.
